A winter tide

Salt water freezes below the freezing point of fresh water.1 Here the winter tide reaches a wall of pale ice twice a day.

A water molecule is written H2O. The small numeral belongs below the line. In the same notebook, an area of one square metre is written 1 m2.

A point on the curve has coordinates x1 and y1. For a square, its area is x2. These labels keep their place beside the letters when the type is enlarged.

1 Salt lowers the temperature at which liquid water and ice can coexist.
